main_body: Thatched hut: a tall stepped thatch roof slope (rows 0-37) over a plank wall with a recessed door and window (rows 38-63)
top_band: Light golden thatch roof slope, rows 1-34, in banded courses. A lighter eave edge at rows 34-35 closes it, with a dark shadow at rows 36-37.
evidence: The roof reads as a large foreshortened slope seen from the south. It is lighter and textured, and a bright eave lip and dark eave shadow separate it from the wall. The wall below is a distinct vertical face with a door set in a dark frame, a window with a sill, and horizontal beams. This matches how the Beodeul house roofs sit above their walls. No receding side face is drawn, and it is not a front elevation, because the roof is a large surface and not a thin band.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 6 lightness steps in banded courses with per-straw grain. The wall planks, door and window carry their own tones and iron straps. Outlines are dark brown, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral. There are no flat 5x5 fills. The median of 8 colours per tile is a little below the references (11 and 18), and 29 distinct colours is low next to 66 and 185. The piece is small and monochrome-ramped, and the structure and shading craft hold up next to the references without looking like a sticker.
